title: Jabash
summary: Jabash is a Shinnecock Neck placename recorded by William Wallace Tooker for a cove on the east side of the neck. one Native resident on the neck called it Irabash cove.
address_label: East side of Shinnecock Neck, Southampton, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate general marker based on Tooker identifying Jabash as a cove on the east side of Shinnecock Neck halfway from the head of the creek to the point; exact cove location remains uncertain.
why_this_matters: Although archaeological investigations have not yet uncovered physical artifacts at the Jabash village site, the fact that an Indigenous trail formed the basis for the modern Montauk Highway underscores a profound historical continuity. Recognizing these original travel routes reminds us that the everyday infrastructure of Long Island was actively carved out and utilized by Native peoples long before European paved roads.
translation_content:
No settled translation is given for Jabash. The main alternate form in his entry is Irabash, used in the phrase Irabash cove.

Why Place Names Matter

“Knowledge was passed directly from Elders to youth through experience, language, and story. Place names carry law, memory, and instruction.”

— Tłı̨chǫ Government, Trails of our Ancestors: Building a Nation (2026), article text
land_loss_content: Jabash keeps a local Shinnecock Neck place-name visible while avoiding false precision for a cove whose exact location remains uncertain. The cove name links Shinnecock Neck to living landscape knowledge and continuing place memory.
whereintheworld_content: The map marker gives a broad orientation to the east side of Shinnecock Neck and should be understood as a general landscape point.
